q: Furstenberg's ergodic proof of Szemerédi's theorem (1977) shows that any A⊆ℤ with positive upper density contains k-term arithmetic progressions by proving:
opts: Multiple recurrence: for any ergodic MPT and B with μ(B)>0, lim inf (1/N)∑ μ(B∩T^{-n}B∩...∩T^{-kn}B) > 0
That A must contain a perfect square
Fourier analysis shows A has large spectrum
exp: Furstenberg's multiple recurrence theorem: for any MPT (X,μ,T) and B with μ(B)>0, ∫ᵢₙf(1/N)∑_{n=1}^N μ(B∩T^{-n}B∩...∩T^{-kn}B)>0. Via the Furstenberg correspondence principle, this gives Szemerédi's theorem.
